title_tag: Nadi Pariksha in Calgary | Ayurvedic Pulse Reading
meta_description: Nadi Pariksha, Ayurvedic pulse reading, in Calgary: what it is, what it can and cannot tell you, and how it fits a consultation. Included in the visit.

data.lead: Nadi Pariksha (pulse reading) is the Ayurvedic practice of reading the radial pulse at the wrist with three fingers to assess constitution and current balance. It is part of every in-person consultation here, not a separate service, and this page is honest about what it is: a traditional assessment, not a diagnostic test.

data.md:
## What happens

You sit comfortably with your arm relaxed. The practitioner places the index, middle and ring fingers on the radial pulse of one wrist, then the other, for a minute or two each, at different pressures. In the tradition, the three finger positions correspond to Vata, Pitta and Kapha, and the quality of the pulse under each (its rhythm, its feel, how it moves) describes the constitution (prakriti) and the current state (vikriti). It is quiet, quick and painless.

## What it can tell you, and what it cannot

In Ayurvedic practice, pulse reading is one input among several: what you tell us, how you look, your tongue and skin, the season. It helps the practitioner choose between, say, a warming routine and a cooling one, or between two oils for Abhyanga. That is useful.

What it is not: a way to detect disease, a substitute for blood tests or imaging, or something that can tell you what is wrong with you. Some Ayurvedic websites claim far more for pulse reading than that; we do not. If anything in the consultation suggests a medical question, the answer is your physician, and we will say so.

## Preparing for it

Come without caffeine for two hours beforehand if you can, not straight after exercise or a heavy meal, and sit quietly for a few minutes first. None of this is essential; it simply makes the reading clearer.

h1: Abhyanga: Ayurvedic Warm Oil Massage in Calgary

data.lead: Abhyanga (warm oil massage) is Ayurveda's full-body massage: warm herbal oil, long rhythmic strokes, and an hour in which nothing is asked of you. Given here by a practitioner trained in Ayurveda in India who is also a Registered Massage Therapist, so the session is receipted as massage therapy.

data.md:
## What Abhyanga is

Abhyanga is the foundation of the therapies on this site. Warm oil, usually sesame-based and chosen for you, is applied over the whole body with strokes that follow the direction of the muscle and circle the joints. The pressure is moderate: enough to work the muscles, light enough that you can drift. Unlike most massage, a great deal of oil is used, and it is left on the skin afterwards rather than wiped away.

In Ayurvedic terms, Abhyanga is the daily counter to Vata, the quality of dryness, cold and movement. It is the therapy the tradition prescribes for a dry climate, a busy mind and a body that sits too much, which describes a good part of Calgary.

## What people come for

Clients commonly book Abhyanga for muscle tension and stiffness, for dry skin through the winter, for sleep that has gone light, and as the monthly hour that keeps them steady. Many pair it with Shirodhara in one visit. It is also the usual first therapy for someone new to Ayurveda, because it needs no preparation and is easy to enjoy.

title_tag: Shirodhara in Calgary | Warm Oil Forehead Therapy
meta_description: Shirodhara in Calgary: warm herbal oil poured in a steady stream over the forehead for deep rest. 60 min $130; 105 min with Abhyanga $230.

data.lead: Shirodhara (warm oil poured steadily over the forehead) is the Ayurvedic therapy people ask for by name. Thirty-five minutes of a thin, warm stream moving slowly across the brow, in a quiet room, with nothing to do. Most clients fall asleep. Given in Calgary by a practitioner trained in Ayurveda in India.

data.md:
## What Shirodhara is

You lie on your back with your eyes covered. A copper vessel with a narrow spout hangs above your forehead. Warm oil, usually a sesame-based herbal oil chosen for you, flows from it in a continuous stream that moves slowly from temple to temple. The vessel is refilled so the stream never breaks. After thirty to thirty-five minutes the oil is worked gently into the scalp and you rest.

In Ayurvedic terms, Shirodhara calms Vata in the head: the racing mind, the light sleep, the feeling of being wound tight. That is the tradition's description, and it matches who tends to book it.

## What the evidence says

Honestly, less than the internet claims. Small studies from India and Japan describe people relaxing and sleeping better after a course of Shirodhara; none has a proper control group. We offer it as a deeply restful therapy that clients value for stress and sleep, not as a treatment for any diagnosed condition. If you are under a physician's care for sleep or mood, keep that care in place; Shirodhara can sit beside it.

h1: Kati Vasti: Warm Oil Therapy for the Lower Back

data.lead: Kati Vasti (warm oil held on the lower back; also spelled Kati Basti) is Ayurveda's answer to a stiff, tired lower back. A ring of dough on the skin, filled with warm herbal oil and kept warm for half an hour. No pressure, no manipulation; warmth and time.

data.md:
## What Kati Vasti is

Kati means the lower back and hips; Vasti means a container. A ring of black-gram or wheat-flour dough is pressed onto the lower back and filled with warm oil, which is drawn off and replaced as it cools so the area stays at a steady warmth throughout. The oil is chosen for you at your consultation.

In Ayurvedic terms, Kati Vasti is a warming, nourishing therapy for an area where Vata has settled: stiffness that is worst in the morning or after sitting, a back that tires rather than one that is sharply injured, the wear of desk work, driving and winter.

## What people come for

Clients commonly report that the back feels warm and loose straight afterwards, that stiffness on getting out of bed is less for a day or two, and that the effect lasts longer with each session in a course of three to five. Many combine it with Abhyanga, or with the stretches and routine set out in a consultation.

The published research on Kati Vasti is thin: small studies and case reports, almost always with other therapies given at the same time. We offer it as a thorough, pleasant way to apply sustained warmth to a sore back, not as a treatment for a back condition. Persistent back pain, pain with numbness or weakness in a leg, pain after a fall, or pain with fever needs your physician first.

## What Janu Vasti is

Janu is the knee. The therapy is the same as Kati Vasti, moved to the joint that carries you up Calgary's hills and stairs: a dough ring is shaped around the knee, filled with warm herbal oil, and the oil is kept warm for 25 to 30 minutes. Both knees can be done in one session.

In Ayurvedic terms the knees are a seat of Vata, which is why they are described as the first joints to feel dry, stiff and noisy with age, cold and overuse. Warm oil, held and not rubbed, is the tradition's response.

## What people come for

Clients commonly book Janu Vasti for knees that are stiff in the morning or after sitting, that feel the cold, or that tire on stairs and walks, and as part of recovering their routine after a long time off their feet. The research on Janu Vasti alone is sparse; we offer it as a comfortable, thorough way to warm the knee, not as a treatment for a knee condition. A knee that is swollen, hot, locking, giving way or injured needs your physician or a physiotherapist first.

data.lead: Nasya (nasal oil therapy) is the Ayurvedic practice of putting a few drops of oil or ghee into the nostrils. This practice does not perform Nasya at the clinic. What we do is explain, in a consultation, how to use nasal oil safely at home, which is the form most Canadians can benefit from in a climate as dry as Calgary's.

data.text: Why we do not perform it: in Alberta, procedures that go beyond the point where the nasal passages narrow are restricted to regulated health professionals, and clinic-administered Nasya can cross that line. Home use of a drop of oil at the opening of the nostril does not. We keep to the side of that line that protects you and us.

data.md:
## What Nasya is, in the tradition

Ayurveda regards the nose as the doorway to the head. Classical Nasya ranges from a single drop of oil at the nostril's edge, done daily as part of the morning routine, to clinic procedures using medicated oils in larger quantities after steam and massage. The daily drop is what we teach; the clinic procedures are not offered here.

## Home nasal oil: the simple version

After your morning shower, warm a drop of plain sesame oil or ghee between clean fingertips and rub it just inside each nostril, no further than the fingertip reaches comfortably. That is all. It takes ten seconds and, in heated winter air, is the difference between a nose that cracks and bleeds and one that does not. Some clients prefer a licensed nasal oil product with a Natural Product Number; we can suggest options.

In a consultation we go through which oil suits you, when in the day to use it, and what to do about the common Calgary complaints of a dry, blocked or stuffy nose and sinus pressure, including steam, hydration, humidity at home, and when it is a physician's job rather than ours.

## Sinus and congestion

People search for Nasya because of sinus trouble. Be clear about what oil can and cannot do: it keeps the lining moist and comfortable; it does not treat a sinus infection. Facial pain with fever, thick coloured discharge, symptoms lasting more than ten days, or sinus trouble that keeps coming back are reasons to see your physician. We will say so in the consultation and send you there.

meta_description: Panchakarma in Calgary as a five-day external program: Abhyanga, Shirodhara, Vasti and herbal steam with diet and routine. $695.

data.lead: Panchakarma (Ayurveda's cleansing program) at Ayurvedachalam is a five-day course of external therapies, warm oil massage, Shirodhara, Vasti and herbal steam, with a simple diet and daily routine for the week. It is the most restful week Ayurveda offers. It does not include any internal procedure, and this page explains why.

data.text: What is not included: classical Panchakarma has five internal procedures (therapeutic vomiting, purgation, enema therapies, nasal administration and bloodletting). None is offered here. In Alberta those procedures are restricted to regulated health professionals, and we would not offer them regardless. Our program is the external preparation and care that surrounds them in the tradition, which is what most people in Canada are looking for when they search for Panchakarma.

data.md:
## The five days

Each day is about 90 minutes at the clinic, at a time that suits you, with the diet and routine carried on at home.

1. **Day 1**: consultation review, Abhyanga (60 min) and herbal steam.
2. **Day 2**: Abhyanga and Shirodhara.
3. **Day 3**: Kati Vasti or Janu Vasti (your choice) and steam.
4. **Day 4**: Abhyanga and Shirodhara.
5. **Day 5**: Abhyanga, steam, and a closing conversation about the routine to keep.

The therapies are chosen with you at a consultation beforehand; a day can be swapped (Pizhichil for Abhyanga, for example) at the practitioner's discretion. Booked separately these sessions come to $845; the program is $695.

## The diet and routine for the week

Warm, simple, mostly cooked food: kitchari (rice and split mung beans with ghee and spices), soups, stewed fruit, warm water through the day. No alcohol, no cold or raw food, early nights, and as little screen time in the evening as you can manage. This is the "cleansing" of the program, in the tradition's sense of the word: a week of rest for the digestion, not a purge. We send the plan in writing before day one.

## When to do it

The tradition favours the change of seasons. In Calgary that means late October to early November, before deep winter, and April, as it lifts. Clients also book it after a hard stretch at work or when sleep has gone. Plan a quiet week; the program does not suit a week of travel or heavy training.
